product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. Under that one product entry point, the two top-level commerce actions are buy and sell: Buyer workflows are available now; Seller workflows will use the same entry point and are not implemented yet.
title: Railway Query, Planning, and Ticket Booking
purpose: Choose the right railway service for the buyer's situation, submit the exact input contract each service expects, and follow the protected booking flow without inventing field names.
when_to_use: The buyer wants train schedules, routes, or tickets.
A railway service execution fails at the geo, search, catalog, or recommend step.
The buyer only knows a city or fuzzy location rather than a station name.
The buyer asks about seat preferences, refunds, or ticket issuance status.

service_selection.itpay-rail-exact: Use when the buyer knows BOTH the exact departure and arrival railway station names (e.g. 古镇 → 广州南). Direct train query, fastest path. Do NOT use it with only a city or fuzzy location.
service_selection.itpay-rail-smart: Use when the buyer has a city name, an area, an address, or wants transfer planning and recommendations. The platform resolves locations to stations itself; never silently convert a city into its namesake station.
service_selection.svc_qizhidao_company_lookup: Not a railway service; do not mix intents.

required.origin: Departure railway station name only, e.g. 古镇. Not a city or an address.
required.destination: Arrival railway station name only, e.g. 广州南.
required.travel_date: Travel date in YYYY-MM-DD. The field name must be exactly travel_date; aliases like date are rejected.

itpay-rail-exact.optional: None. additionalProperties is false — extra fields are rejected by the provider.

required.origin: Fullest known departure location: city, district, area, or address is all acceptable.
required.destination: Fullest known arrival location, same rule as origin.
required.travel_date: Travel date in YYYY-MM-DD. The field name must be exactly travel_date.

optional.origin_city: Departure city hint that helps location resolution.
optional.depart_after: Do not depart before this time.
optional.arrive_before: Do not arrive after this time.
optional.priority: One of balanced | fastest | cheapest | safest | flexible.

flow: services start <service> --json returns input_required plus the guidance block for rail services.
Submit input with services run <service> --execution <id> --input-json <file> --json on the SAME execution.
itpay-rail-smart may stop at a location confirmation step; show the candidate places to the buyer, then continue the same execution after the human confirms.
After a train and seat are chosen, the booking flow moves to a protected checkout page: passenger identity data is entered by the human on that page, never through the CLI.
Payment success does not mean the ticket is issued. Issuance is asynchronous; keep reading the same execution with services next.
If seat details are still syncing after issuance, advise the buyer to verify the itinerary on 12306 instead of repeating the query.

failure_handling.failed_step: The CLI reports failed_step and failed_step_meaning in the result when a workflow fails.
failure_handling.geo: Location resolution failed: check origin/destination are real place names, or attach origin_city/coordinate hints, then start a NEW execution (a failed execution is terminal).
failure_handling.search: Supplier query failed: most commonly a wrong field name (must be travel_date) or a nonexistent station name; recheck input against this doc.
failure_handling.catalog_or_recommend: Location resolved but no feasible trains: change the date or stations.
failure_handling.general_rule: Never replay a failed execution and never guess different field names; correct the input and start a new execution of the same service.

seat_preferences.meaning: A buyer's seat-letter preference may be planned per leg before payment. The plan is submitted to the supplier when encodable; unsupported combinations fall back to automatic assignment.
seat_preferences.letters: Evidence-backed letters only: O=ABCDF (second class), M=ACDF (first class), 9=ACF (business class). Other layouts auto-assign.
seat_preferences.boundary: Never claim a preference was fulfilled before supplier confirmation; check the issued seat in the order/status output.

agent_rules: Pick the service by the buyer's input precision: exact station names → itpay-rail-exact; anything fuzzier → itpay-rail-smart.
Never invent input field names. If the guidance block or this doc does not list a field, do not send it.
Never ask the buyer for passenger names, ID numbers, or phone numbers in chat; those are collected only on the protected checkout page.
Do not repeat or replay a failed execution; correct the input and start a new one.
Do not claim payment equals ticket issuance; issuance is asynchronous and confirmed only by the issued seat status.
